concept.name: Exchange reserve
concept.definition: Exchange reserve (exchange balance) is the total amount of a coin held in wallets attributed to centralized exchanges — the immediately sellable inventory sitting on trading venues.
concept.intuition: It is the stock of goods on shop shelves: a bulging shelf means plenty of potential supply for sale; emptying shelves mean holders have taken their coins home.
concept.mechanics: Analytics firms cluster and label exchange addresses and track their aggregate balance over time; reserves fall when outflows exceed inflows (accumulation/cold-storage trend) and rise when inflows dominate (distribution risk). Glassnode documented BTC exchange balances dropping ~7% from their February 2020 high as post-crash withdrawals outpaced deposits.
concept.formula: Exchange reserve_t = Σ balances of labeled exchange addresses; Δreserve ≈ inflow − outflow.
concept.failure_modes: Label coverage is incomplete and changes as exchanges rotate wallets, so levels and trends embed attribution error; reserves also embed coins that will never be sold (market-maker inventory), and reserve trends can invert during exchange insolvencies for non-bullish reasons.
concept.misconceptions: Falling reserves are not mechanically bullish — they can reflect loss of trust in a venue (FTX-style runs) or migration to other custodians. Reserves measure potential, not actual, sell pressure.
concept.example: If labeled exchange wallets hold 2.4M BTC out of ~19.9M supply, roughly 12% of all coins sit as venue inventory; a slide to 2.0M over a year of net outflows signals tightening liquid supply.

citations.source: Glassnode Insights - The Number of BTC On Exchanges Is Down Almost 7%
